headline: H-EAR forces the Galois PAIR {SU(3)_2 kappa=5, SU(5)_1 kappa=6}, NOT kappa=5; kappa=5 is a priced choice -- the price is one orientation bit (the 1/phi branch / E6-cusp-end anchor / minimal kappa).
discriminating_fact: The shadow-realization predicate H-EAR has EXACTLY TWO solutions -- SU(3)_2 (kappa=5, value 1/phi) and SU(5)_1 (kappa=6, value phi) -- the two Galois conjugates (sqrt5<->-sqrt5) of ONE golden doublet, BOTH genuine conductor-5 hearings (Part 3). SU(6)_1 (kappa=7) is excluded exactly by two walls (projective T-order 4!=5; sqrt5 not in Q(zeta24)). kappa=5 is singled out only by an EXTRA principle -- cusp-field match Q(sqrt-3)=A2 (Part 4) or, equivalently, re-invoked minimality -- and that principle chooses one side of a Z/2 the theta-symmetric object does not itself break (non-canonicity, banked). Hence kappa=5 is forced only up to the Galois pair; the last step is a priced choice, not a theorem.
